note: Track note-names, step 2: sharps and flats as the black key beside a white one, then one sharp in G major and one flat in F major on the staff, each ringed where the text names it. The keys are the lesson, so there are no moves, and each section has a feel to reach. Missing: piano-keys marks only the notes of its scale, so the black keys carry no names and the C♯ / D♭ the text names is not lit; no tool shows one black key under both of its names.

exercise.title: Sharps and flats
exercise.why: A sharp is the next key to the right on the piano and a flat is the next key to the left, so every black key gets its name from the white key beside it.

cells.text:
On the piano below, tap {{c}}, then the black key just to its right: that is {{c-sharp}}, a half step higher. Now tap {{d}}, then the same black key: from this side it is {{d-flat}}, a half step lower.
Go along the other black keys the same way, and say both names of each.
Practice until both names of a black key come without counting from C.

The staff below shows G major, a scale that needs one sharp. Tap up from {{1}} and say each letter: the ringed note is {{f-sharp}}, not F.
Then tap {{f-sharp}} and the {{1}} above it: they are a half step apart.
Practice until you say F♯ as you tap it, not after.

The staff below shows F major, a scale that needs one flat. Tap up from {{1}} and say each letter: the ringed note is {{b-flat}}, not B.
Then tap {{3}} and {{b-flat}}: they are a half step apart too.
Practice until you say B♭ as you tap it, not after.
